name: Independent-Kinetic Screened-Frame Decoupling
claimed_mechanism: A multiplier field K carries its own standard kinetic term and fixes the finite normalization of the propagating chi mode. The preferred-frame response is isolated in a lapse-weighted coupling to the khronon u that is multiplied by e^-y, so it is screened in high-density regimes. This architecture keeps mu(y)=1-e^-y frozen and leaves matter minimally coupled to the single physical metric.
predicted_weak_field: In the unscreened low-density limit, e^-y is order unity and the preferred-frame term contributes the expected MOND acceleration scale through the auxiliary chi Legendre structure. In the screened high-density limit, the preferred-frame term is suppressed while the K-normalized chi kinetic term remains finite, preventing the P7 collision between alpha and kinetic normalization. The weak-field metric perturbation therefore retains a finite propagating mode with a screened preferred-frame response.
inequivalence_argument: This is not constraint-first because the chi mode is not algebraically eliminated and retains a finite propagating kinetic sector. It is not screened-preferred-frame because the screened e^-y factor appears only in the preferred-frame coupling, not in the kinetic normalization. It is not spatially-nonlocal or multi-sector because all interactions are local and there is one physical metric with one auxiliary chi sector. It is not degenerate because K has a standard kinetic term and independently fixes the propagating-mode normalization.
